task_request: I am a calculus instructor, and I want to produce a teaching materials package on the concept of derivatives for my introductory calculus students. (1) Create an animation derivatives_animation.mp4 showing: the function f(x)=x² at the point x=1, where a secant line progressively approaches the tangent line as h decreases from 2 down to 0.01. Dynamically display the slope value as it changes, and annotate the final derivative f'(1)=2. Then show f(x)=sin(x) with its derivative f'(x)=cos(x) overlaid on the same axes. (2) Create a companion teaching handout derivatives_slides.pdf (at least 8 pages) covering: definition of a derivative, limit formula, geometric interpretation, common derivative formulas table, chain rule, and application examples.

nodes.objective: Design a coherent introductory lesson connecting the limit definition, secant-to-tangent geometry, common derivative formulas, chain rule, applications, and the relationship between sin(x) and cos(x). Specify an at-least-eight-page handout arc and synchronized animation beats.

Create derivatives_animation.mp4: animate f(x)=x^2 at x=1 with a secant approaching the tangent as h decreases from 2 to 0.01, dynamically display slope, annotate f'(1)=2, then overlay sin(x) and cos(x) with clear labels and pacing.

Create derivatives_slides.pdf with at least eight pages covering definition, limit formula, geometry, common formulas table, chain rule, worked applications and a summary, with notation and visuals consistent with the animation.

Inspect both outputs for exact filenames, playable animation content, slope/tangent and sin/cos stages, handout page count and section coverage, notation consistency and readability. Report without changes.
